A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same readable 11-page BTP paper, supporting reliable comparison of text, equations, tables and figures. Neither contains an appendix; both refer to supplementary material absent from the supplied files.

before.justification: v2 reports original BTP experiments on Real3D-AD and Anomaly-ShapeNet, including benchmark results, cross-category evaluation and ablations in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original BTP benchmark results, cross-category experiments, ablations and qualitative localization results in Section 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Figure 2 retain identical encoding, GFCM, MGFEM, hybrid prompts, anomaly scoring and joint local/global/geometric training objectives.

E1.justification: Both evaluate object-level anomaly detection and point-level localization on Real3D-AD and Anomaly-ShapeNet, with identical category coverage and cross-category scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1 and 3, including PointAD, AnomalyCLIP, PointCLIPV2, M3DM and PatchCore variants. Figure 3 retains the same M3DM, PointCore and aligned ULIP comparisons.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same metrics, single-category training and cross-category testing protocol, 2,048-point preprocessing, ULIP2 backbone and optimization settings.

E4.justification: The cross-category analysis in Table 2, module and loss ablations in Table 4, input-point sensitivity study in Table 5 and qualitative comparisons in Figure 3 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both state that results average 10 independent runs with different random seeds in Section 4.2. Table 3 retains identical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1–5 and Figure 3 are unchanged. BTP's object/point AUROC remains 61.4%/84.5% on Real3D-AD and 65.2%/87.3% on Anomaly-ShapeNet in Table 3.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), including feature definitions, fusion and loss formulations, are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about direct PLM-based zero-shot detection, multi-granularity alignment, joint representation learning and empirical performance.

C2.justification: Sections 4–5 retain the same interpretations of localization strength, weaker object-level detection, cross-category transfer and module complementarity, together with the same proposed future scoring improvements.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including prompt length, selected encoder layers, optimizer schedule, loss weights, RTX 4090 hardware and PyTorch version. The prospective code-release statement and repository link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 58 references are unchanged, including the positioning against projection-based methods and PLANE's target-category adaptation.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp text changes from v2 dated 8 June 2026 to v3 dated 12 July 2026. The title, authors, prose, terminology and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: The vertical arXiv stamp shifts downward and slightly right on page 1. The remaining first-page content and pages 2–11 render identically; all figures, tables, captions and body layout are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The supplied PDFs differ only in the arXiv version/date stamp and its placement. Scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information and substantive presentation are identical, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
